chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
Love your friend moderately, for it is possible that he may become your enemy one day; and hate your enemy moderately, for it is possible that he may become your friend one day.
ai.seo_question: How should one balance love and hatred in personal relationships according to Shia ethics?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) advises maintaining a moderate degree of love and hatred, warning against extremes because social dynamics are fluid and relationships can shift unexpectedly. This teaching reflects the Shia emphasis on *wasatiyyah* (balance) in interpersonal conduct, encouraging emotional restraint to preserve harmony and avoid regret when allegiances change. It serves as a practical guide for navigating the complexities of human relationships with wisdom and foresight.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 268. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:
Have love for your friend up to a limit, for it is possible that he may turn into your enemy some day; and hate your enemy up to a limit for it is possible that he may turn into your friend some day.
